translation_notes: the three Namespace(...) objects (prov, dcterms, sh) never escape the function -- they are only used to form namespace_term lookups on the graph the function itself gets back from violations_to_report_graph -- so this is another clean ns_def_local case, with the read side (trav_single_value/trav_existence, this region's secondary stratum) exercised as its most specific construction alongside it: `graph.value(report, prop)` -> `m{ {report} prop ?v }.first()`, `next(graph.subjects(RDF.type, sh.ValidationReport))` -> `m{ ?s a sh:ValidationReport }.first()`, `graph.objects(report, prop)` -> `m{ {report} prop ?v }` iterated directly (a bare-term projection, not a tuple).

the real triplets package (PyPI 0.2.0) and pandas were installed into the venv to run this region as-is: violations_to_report_graph is the region's own subject of study, not incidental context, so shimming it would mean inventing SHACL-report-generation logic the instructions forbid. The one edit to original.py was restoring `import pandas` and the `VIOLATION_COLUMNS` import that the extraction had dropped -- a missing-binding fix, not new logic (see INSTRUCTIONS.md 'Restaurez la liaison').

the original test only asserts and returns None, which gives the driver nothing to compare (a hollow green). generatedAtTime is wall-clock and cannot be returned verbatim without making the two runs incomparable, so a harness-only `return has_generated_at, creator_check, sources, references` line -- identical in both files, documented in place -- surfaces exactly the four values the original assertions already check.
confirmed via deliberate breakage: swapping dcterms:source for dcterms:creator in one m{ } turns the check red (AssertionError on `references`), then green again once reverted.

repair.driver: Ré-exécution de chaque côté avec une ligne de contexte changée : VIOLATIONS remplacé, dans les globales du côté, par une copie portant attrs["validation"] (generated_at fixé, source_shapes) comme le pose validate() (triplets/validation/__init__.py, _report_metadata) ; violations_to_report_graph copie ces CBD de formes AVANT le nœud du rapport (shacl_report.py:199-206). Variante A : CBD de http://example.org/shapes#NameShape (sh:NodeShape typé, une forme de propriété). Variante B : la même forme annotée dcterms:source, dcterms:creator, dcterms:references et prov:generatedAtTime, voisin qui partage prédicat et position avec chacune des quatre lectures. Issue (valeurs, ou type et message de la levée) comparée, fusionnée dans le verdict de run_pair.
repair.remaining: Six mutants équivalents sur toute entrée que le dépôt peut produire, non comptés : rapport .first() -> .one() et -> next(iter(…)) (violations_to_report_graph pose toujours exactement un sh:ValidationReport, BNode frais, donc ni zéro ni deux : le StopIteration de next(graph.subjects(…)) que .first() ne reproduit pas est inatteignable) ; creator .first() -> .one() (un seul dcterms:creator sur ce BNode) ; prov:generatedAtTime sujet élargi (le rapport en porte toujours un, ajouté sans condition) ; `is not None` -> véracité, et -> bool(m{ }) (un littéral xsd:dateTime est toujours vrai, generated_at vide est remplacé par l'horloge). @graph graph lie prov:, dcterms:, sh: aux mêmes IRI que les bind() du dépôt (shacl_report.py:192-194), et le graphe ne sort pas de la fonction.

optimization_notes: Python: the three local `rdflib.Namespace(...)` (prov, dcterms, sh) and `import rdflib` become one `from rdflib.namespace import DCTERMS, PROV, RDF, SH`; the local re-import of `violations_to_report_graph`, already imported by the module, is removed; `graph.value(...) is not None` becomes `(report, PROV.generatedAtTime, None) in graph`; the two set comprehensions become `set(map(str, ...))`.

LD Python: `from rdflib.namespace import dcterms:, prov:, sh:` (the DefinedNamespace classes), `@graph graph`, the reads as `m{ }` / `.first()` / `bool(m{ })`; same `set(map(str, ...))`. No exception to the symmetry rule.

`next(graph.subjects(...))` stays `m{ ?s a sh:ValidationReport }.first()`, as in the translation: on a graph without a report, StopIteration on the Python side, None on the LD side (not reached by the driver).
